subject: EdgeCloud - VPC egress scenarios & log/retention follow-up
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Arnaud Lefevre <arnaud@edgecloud.io>, Elaine Moore <elaine@edgecloud.io>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: EdgeCloud - VPC egress scenarios & log/retention follow-up

Hi Arnaud / Elaine —

Thanks again for the productive call today. Quick recap and the asks we committed to:

- Primary constraints we heard: customer PII must not leave their VPC unless encrypted and subject to retention rules; any outbound egress needs to be tightly scoped and auditable.
- EdgeCloud prefers private connectivity (VPC Peering or PrivateLink) to Redwood Dedicated or Private control plane; an air-gap for certain environments may be required for later phases.
- Logging: access/audit logs must be retained for 12 months with a copy exported to the customer's log archiving bucket in their account.
- Data residency: model inference raw inputs (containing PII) should be processed in the us-east-1 region only. Metadata-only telemetry can be aggregated cross-region.

Attachments: I attached a short SOC2 summary you requested and an initial proposed dataflow diagram (SVG).

Immediate next steps (we'll do these by EOD Tuesday unless you want to adjust):
1) Rishi and Ben will map two deployment options (Private deployment inside your VPC using Private Control Plane vs Dedicated pools with VPC peering/PrivateLink).
2) We’ll provide a short table showing where logs live, retention policy, and which logs we export to your bucket.
3) Please confirm whether TLS termination must occur in your VPC or if mutual TLS to Redwood's control plane is acceptable for control-plane messaging.

If there are any errors in my notes, flag them and I’ll correct. Otherwise expect the deployment options doc from Rishi and a logging export sketch from Ben.

Thanks —
Laura

Laura —

Thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side:

- Confirmed: PII (names, email, phone, customer identifiers) cannot be persisted outside our account in cleartext. Transient processing is allowed if data is encrypted in transit and at rest; we need assurance keys are customer-controlled (KMS) for the private deployment.
- Retention: 12 months for audit logs, but we also need a 30-day hot retention for inference request traces that our SOC might need to query quickly. Can you scope log export cadence (near-real-time vs batch)?
- Egress: For the Initial PoC we prefer a private link to a Redwood Dedicated pool in our VPC. For the longer term, some teams may explore an air-gapped on-prem option — we'll discuss timing later.

I'll have our security engineer (cc: security@edgecloud.io) validate the SOC2 summary and the SVG; they may come back with a few KMS/crypto questions.

Regards,
Arnaud

Looping the infra/ops questions here so we can produce the two option matrix:

1) KMS / key ownership
   - Option A (Private deployment): Customer-managed KMS/HSM in their account. Keys never leave customer account; Redwood only has wrapped keys for any control-plane metadata.
   - Option B (Dedicated pool): We can support customer KMS via External Key Management (EKM) or a cross-account decrypt proxy; need to check if customer requires HSM-backed keys for runtime.

2) Log export cadence / format
   - We can export audit logs in near-real-time (pub/sub -> customer bucket) or in daily batches. For 30-day hot access, recommend near-real-time with a short-term index in customer's Elasticsearch cluster (we can push).

3) Egress paths
   - PrivateLink: minimal NAT/egress risk, control-plane still needs a management channel to Redwood (mutual TLS).
   - VPC Peering: simpler network topology; ensure no transitive routing to other Redwood accounts.
   - On-prem/air-gap: needs offline bundle of the runtime + signed model artifacts and an operator-run control channel (manual updates).

Action items for our deliverable:
- Rishi: produce a concise two-column matrix (Private deployment vs Dedicated) with columns: network connectivity, key ownership, log flow, retention options, expected SLO impact.
- Ben: produce recommended log export architecture and sample retention policies (hot 30d, cold 12mo).
- Laura: confirm whether we should include an explicit 'no-PII-exfiltration' clause for the PoC SOW.

I'll draft the matrix by EOD Tuesday and attach the sample retention policy.

-Ben

Arnaud / Elaine —

Appreciate the quick clarifications. A couple of commitments from our side based on Ben's note below:

- We'll include KMS options in the matrix and mark customer-managed KMS as the default for Private deployment. If EdgeCloud needs HSM-backed keys for runtime, we'll flag that as a requirement and note potential lead time.
- Log export: we can support near-real-time export via a secure stream to your bucket + 30-day hot index (we'll provide specifics and a cost estimate).
- Egress: for the PoC we recommend PrivateLink into a Dedicated pool (minimizes network complexity); we will include the Private deployment option in the same doc for reference.
- PoC SOW: we'll include a short 'no-PII exfiltration' clause and an appendix describing retention/exports.

Next steps / timeline:
- Tue EOD (PST): Ben to share retention policy draft and sample export flow.
- Wed noon (PST): Rishi to share the 2-option matrix and recommended configuration for PrivateLink (network steps, required IAM roles).
- Wed EOD: Laura to consolidate and send a single OnePager + next-step checklist to EdgeCloud (drive link included).

Arnaud — can you confirm whether EdgeCloud security wants the export to be delivered over VPC endpoints only (preferred) or if S3 signed PUT with VPC Gateway endpoints is acceptable? That will affect our proposed architecture.

Thanks,
Laura
